chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
The ones sitting around the man are participants in the gift.
ai.seo_question: Who shares in a gift given to a person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the etiquette of social reciprocity, establishing that companions present during a gift-giving occasion are entitled to a share, thereby preventing jealousy and strengthening communal bonds. This principle reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining harmony (sulh) within the circle of friends and ensuring that generosity is perceived as inclusive rather than exclusive. It serves as a practical guideline for social interactions, reinforcing the idea that gifts are not merely personal transactions but acts of social solidarity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form one of his companions, from Aban, from Ibrahim Bin Umar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘The ones sitting around the man are participants in the gift’.
